title: The Promise Stands
subtitle: The Hour is not a possibility. It is an appointment.
sources: Qur'an 33:63 — 'People ask you concerning the Hour. Say, Knowledge of it is only with Allah'
Qur'an 20:15 — 'Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it - so that every soul may be recompensed according to that for which it strives'

chapters.heading: Almost Concealed
chapters.body: The Qur'an states the end of the world the way calendars state the seasons — as settled fact: 'Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it - so that every soul may be recompensed according to that for which it strives' (20:15). Almost concealed: close enough to shape every choice, far enough that no one builds a business on the date. The Prophet ﷺ said the Hour and his own sending were joined like these two fingers — and a hadith in Sahih Muslim (number not re-checked here) lists ten major signs, each a catastrophe with a name. The mercy of the design is in the concealment: had the date been known, the last generation would inherit everything and earn nothing; had it been deniable, no one would prepare. So it stays almost — the appointment on the wall with no hour beneath it, and the entire art of faith is living ready for a knock that has no schedule.
chapters.label: Hadith report (reference not checked)

familyQuestion: The date is hidden but the appointment is certain. How would you spend this week if the knock came Friday?

title: The Moon Split
subtitle: The first great sign the Qur'an itself named
sources: Qur'an 54:1-2 — 'The Hour has come near, and the moon has split [in two]'
Reports of the Makkans asking for a sign (hadith and seerah; collection, number and source not checked here)

chapters.heading: And They Saw It
chapters.body: The Qur'an opens Surah Al-Qamar with it: 'The Hour has come near, and the moon has split [in two]. And if they see a miracle, they turn away and say, Passing magic' (54:1-2). The reports (in the hadith collections and the seerah; numbers and sources not checked here) say that the people of Makkah asked for a sign and the moon was seen in two parts, one part over the mountain — and the verse names what followed: they called it passing magic. The verse frames denial not as ignorance of the sign, but as refusal of its meaning. A miracle is not evidence for those committed to unbelief; the moon can split and the witness can shrug. Signs ask something of the heart before they ask anything of the eyes.
chapters.label: Seerah report (source not checked)

familyQuestion: They saw the moon split and called it magic. What have you seen with your own eyes that you're explaining away?

title: The Minor Signs
subtitle: The syllabus of the centuries — read as milestones, not dates
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari, number not re-checked — 'time will pass rapidly... the barefoot naked will compete in building tall structures'
Sahih Muslim, number not re-checked — knowledge lifted, ignorance paraded
Qur'an 81:1-14 — the surah of the falling signs

chapters.heading: Knowledge Lifted
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ mapped the centuries in single sentences, and the hadith collections preserve the map: time will compress until a year passes like a month, a month like a week (Bukhari 1036); knowledge will be lifted and ignorance will rule — meaning the knowledgeable dying and the ignorant leading (Bukhari, number not re-checked); drinking and music will spread until generations are raised on them; the barefoot and naked will compete in the height of buildings (Bukhari, number not re-checked); a man will obey his wife and disobey his mother, and treat his friend and abandon his father (Tirmidhi 2210, daif per Darussalam). Each generation has read the list and seen its own decade in it — which is precisely the design: the signs are not a countdown but a curriculum, issued so that every century would find its warnings addressed to it personally. The minor signs end where Surah At-Takwir ends: 'So where are you going? It is not except a reminder to the worlds' (81:26-27). The signs are not there to date the Hour. They are there to wake the sleeper.
chapters.label: Hadith report (reference not checked)

familyQuestion: Every generation found its own decade in the list. Which lines describe your decade most exactly?

title: The Ten Major Signs
subtitle: The ten signs named in the hadith — the report does not fix their order
sources: Sahih Muslim, number not re-checked — the ten signs: Dajjal, descent of Isa, Ya'juj-Ma'juj, three sinkings, smoke, the Beast, sunrise from the west, fire (the order is not stated)
Reported saying — signs following one another like beads (collection and number not checked here; earlier attributed here to Muslim without a number)

chapters.heading: One After Another
chapters.body: The hadith of Hudhayfa ibn Asid names ten great signs (Muslim; number not re-checked here): the Dajjal; the descent of Isa son of Maryam; the release of Ya'juj and Ma'juj; three great sinkings of the earth — east, west, and Arabia; the Smoke; the Beast; the sunrise from the west; and a Fire that drives mankind to their gathering. The report names them without stating the order in which they come, so this card does not claim one. A saying often quoted says they will follow one another 'like beads falling from a string' (reported; collection and number not checked here). Take the comfort that is buried in the list in whatever order they come: after the Dajjal comes Isa, and the Fire is the last road to the gathering for judgment itself.
chapters.label: Hadith report (reference not checked)

familyQuestion: The signs come in order, each bigger than the last. If the syllabus is ordered, what should you learn first?

title: The Smoke
subtitle: Forty days that cover the believer and touch the disbeliever
sources: Qur'an 44:10-11 — 'Then watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke. Covering the people; this is a painful torment'
Report of its effect: believers like a cold, disbelievers smothered (collection not verified; earlier attributed here to Bukhari without a number)

chapters.heading: A Filter in the Sky
chapters.body: 'Then watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke. Covering the people; this is a painful torment' (44:10-11). A report describes its effect: for the believer it touches like a cold — nothing more — 'but for the disbeliever it is like being smothered, coming from every opening of his body' (reported; the collection and number are not checked here, and the forty days sometimes mentioned are not verified either). One sky, two weathers: the same covering that is barely a nuisance to faith is a suffocation to rejection. The smoke is a preview of the judgment itself, where the identical event — standing before the same Lord — is mercy for one soul and anguish for another, and the difference was never the event. The Hour's signs don't create the two kinds of people. They simply stop letting them hide from the difference.
chapters.label: Hadith report (reference not checked)

familyQuestion: The same smoke is a sniffle for one and smothering for the other. What 'same event' are you and someone else experiencing in opposite weathers right now?

title: The Beast
subtitle: A speaker from the earth marking every soul
sources: Qur'an 27:82 — 'And when the word befalls them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth speaking to them'
Sahih Muslim, number not re-checked — the Beast among the ten signs (no further detail from the hadith is given on this card)

chapters.heading: The Earth's Witness
chapters.body: 'And when the word befalls them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth speaking to them, [saying] that the people were' (27:82). Hadith reports add that it will mark people so that believer and disbeliever are told apart (collections, numbers and grades not checked here, so no further detail is given). The Qur'an's own phrasing is the lesson: the Beast 'speaks to them' — the earth itself becomes a witness when the people would not hear the prophets. And the timing in the sequence matters: the Beast comes late, when the arguments have all been made and the denials have all hardened. Some hearts only understand when the ground they stood on rises and speaks.
chapters.label: Hadith report (reference not checked)

familyQuestion: The earth itself will testify. What is the ground of your life saying about you right now — before it has to speak?

title: The Sun Rises from the West
subtitle: The door that closes with the light
sources: Qur'an 6:158 — 'The Day that some of the signs of your Lord will come no soul will benefit from its faith as long as it had not believed before or had earned through its faith some good'
Sahih Muslim, number not re-checked — the sunrise from the west as a major sign
Sahih al-Bukhari, number not re-checked — no repentance accepted after it

chapters.heading: When Seeing Stops Counting
chapters.body: The order of nature is the last argument: 'The Day that some of the signs of your Lord will come no soul will benefit from its faith as long as it had not believed before or had earned through its faith some good' (6:158). The hadith names the sign: the sun rises from the west — the direction of the whole creation reversed in a single morning — and with that reversal, the door of repentance is closed until the Judgment (Bukhari, number not re-checked). Read together, every sign before this one is a summons, and this one is the deadline — after it, seeing is believing and believing no longer avails, because the trial was built for the unseen. 'And it is He who has made the night and the day in succession for whoever desires to remember or desires gratitude' (25:62) — the alternation itself was the proof, repeated every twenty-four hours, free of charge, for a lifetime. The sunrise will simply be the morning the proof stops being subtle.
chapters.label: Hadith report (reference not checked)

familyQuestion: The sun rises from the west only when it's too late. What are you treating as 'too subtle' that is actually your daily proof?

title: The Forty Days of the Dajjal
subtitle: Forty days that test every soul alive
sources: Sahih Muslim 2937 — the Dajjal's itinerary: forty days, one like a year, one like a month, one like a week, the rest like your days
Sahih al-Bukhari, number not re-checked — 'there was no prophet but he warned his people'

chapters.heading: Forty Days of Fire and Rain
chapters.body: The hadith draws the forty days in detail: the Dajjal stays forty days — one day like a year, one like a month, one like a week, and the rest like your days — and he travels every highway except Makkah and Madinah, which the angels turn him from; with him is a garden and a fire, and his fire is coolness and his garden is flame (Muslim 2937). His temptations are not crude: he brings provision to those who follow him and famine to those who refuse — the economics of obedience inverted, as if the whole test of life were run in forty accelerated days. And the Prophet ﷺ said: since the creation of Adam there has been no fitnah like the fitnah of the Dajjal (Muslim 2946) — the concentration of every trial humanity has ever known, compressed into one figure, for forty days. The exit was given before the trial was: al-Kahf's first and last verses, memorized before his arrival, and the Prophet ﷺ said: he will not harm whoever recites them (Muslim, number not re-checked). The greatest test in history came with its answer key, published fourteen centuries early.

familyQuestion: The greatest trial came with its answer key. Do you know the first and last verses of al-Kahf by heart yet?

title: The Descent of Isa
subtitle: The return the prophets promised and the Qur'an sealed
sources: Qur'an 4:157-159 — 'And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in Jesus before his death'
Sahih al-Bukhari 2476 — the descent, the cross broken, the Qur'an ruling
Sahih Muslim 2937 — Isa kills the Dajjal at the gate of Ludd

chapters.heading: He Descends at the White Minaret
chapters.body: The hadith fixes the scene: Isa son of Maryam descends at the white minaret in the eastern part of the Damascus mosque, his hands resting on the wings of two angels (Muslim 2937). He comes not to begin a new revelation but to complete this one: he breaks the cross, kills the swine, abolishes the jizyah — no one left to pay it, all either believing or perishing — and rules by this Qur'an as a Muslim among Muslims (Bukhari 2476), praying behind a leader from among the Muslims — the report does not name that leader. His first act of judgment is the Dajjal's end: at the gate of Ludd in Palestine, Isa catches him, and the narration says the Dajjal melts like salt in water at the sight of him — or dissolves by Isa's spear (Muslim 2937). The Qur'an sealed the theology in advance: 'And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in Jesus before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be against them a witness' (4:159). The world's longest argument ends with the living Witness standing among them.

familyQuestion: Isa returns to rule by the Qur'an. What does it mean that every road in history ends at the same Book?

title: Ya'juj and Ma'juj Released
subtitle: The wall stands by decree; the release is scheduled
sources: Qur'an 18:98 — 'when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level'
Qur'an 21:96-97 — 'from every elevation, descend And [when] the true promise has approached'

chapters.heading: Level Ground
chapters.body: 'Until when [the dam of] Gog and Magog has been opened and they, from every elevation, descend And [when] the true promise has approached; then suddenly the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring' (21:96-97). The hadith fills the release with sound: every day the hordes tunnel at the wall, and every evening their leader says: come back tomorrow — and each day the tunnel is restored, until the day he says — in Allah's name, we will finish it tomorrow — and returns to find the wall like it was (Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3153 — hasan gharib per al-Tirmidhi, sahih per Darussalam; Sunan Ibn Majah 4080 — sahih per Darussalam). Ibn Kathir, as reported by Ma'ariful Qur'an, doubted that this report goes back to the Prophet ﷺ; see Go deeper. The sentence history repeats in al-Kahf's daily recitation — 'but when the promise of my Lord comes' (18:98) — becomes the event. Their surge, the tradition says, drains Lake Tiberias; Isa and the believers withdraw to Mount Tur; and the ending is sudden and strange: Allah sends a worm in their necks, and by morning they are all dead — a nation that terrified the world dies in one night by the smallest of creatures (Muslim 2937). The loudest trial in the sequence ends in silence.

familyQuestion: A nation that terrified the world died in one night by a worm. What giant in your life is smaller than it looks?

title: The Breeze and the Fire
subtitle: A wind, a fire, and the gathering
sources: Sahih Muslim, number not re-checked — the fire as the tenth sign
Qur'an 50:42 — 'The Day they will hear the blast [of the Horn] in truth'
Qur'an 39:68-69 — the two blasts and the earth shining with its Lord's light

chapters.heading: A Wind from the East
chapters.body: After the sinkings, after the smoke, after the Beast and the reversed sun and the returned Isa and the dead hordes — the last sign is the gathering: reports speak of a fire that drives people toward their place of assembly (Muslim, number not re-checked here) and of a wind that takes the souls of the believers; this card does not try to join them into one scene. Then, in the Qur'an, the silence: 'And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills' (39:68). And after the silence, the second blast: 'and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten' (36:51). The fire that gathers them is the last sign because it delivers them to the appointment itself — the plain where, the Qur'an says, 'And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the record [of deeds] will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them in truth' (39:69).
chapters.label: Hadith report (reference not checked)

familyQuestion: The gathering is the last sign because it's the first moment of the meeting. Ready or not — what's your status?

title: The End of the Story
subtitle: The kingdom that never ends
sources: Qur'an 39:69-70 — 'and it will be judged between them in truth, and they will not be wronged'
Qur'an 21:104 — 'The Day when We will fold the heaven like the folding of a [written] sheet for the records'
Qur'an 98:8 — 'Their reward with Allah will be gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow'

chapters.heading: Folding the Sky
chapters.body: The Qur'an ends the world the way a scribe ends a scroll: 'The Day when We will fold the heaven like the folding of a [written] sheet for the records. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. [That is] a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it' (21:104). Then the judgment: 'And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the record [of deeds] will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them in truth, and they will not be wronged' (39:69). And then the story that outlasts the sky itself opens: 'Their reward with Allah will be gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever, Allah being pleased with them and they with Him. That is for whoever has feared his Lord' (98:8). The Last Day is not the end of the story; it is the end of the chapter titled *Trial*. The book it opens has no final page — 'a promise binding upon Us; indeed, We will do it' (21:104). Every sign in this shelf exists to make that page reachable.

familyQuestion: The world ends like a folded scroll — and the next book has no last page. Which book are you writing your page for right now?
